utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can you call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you and good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-R77.1, the Prosecutor versus Zuhdija Tabakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please, microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Oh, was it off? I'm sorry. Mr. Tabakovic, can you hear and understand what we are saying here in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you repeat your answer, please. I don't think the interpreters got that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Appearing for the Prosecution: Peter Kremer; to my right, Kyle Wood; and we're assisted this afternoon by our case manager, Jasmina Bosnjakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of Mr. Tabakovic, my name is Steven Powles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I raise one matter just before we start, and it's in relation to private-session proceedings. I understand that the indictment may be put in its entirety to Mr. Tabakovic in private session. May I also ask on his behalf that if any sensitive matters in addition to the indictment are to be dealt with during the course of these proceedings, if they could also be dealt with in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We'll see about that. The indictment will be read -- if that's necessary, will be read in private session, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: I'm very grateful, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tabakovic, under the Statute and the Rules of the Tribunal, you have the right to remain silent at all times during the proceedings. You have also been assigned counsel in this case, duty counsel. Now I have to ask you: Are you satisfied with the counsel assigned to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you received a copy of the indictment in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Has counsel explained the indictment against you and the charges against you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You have the right to have the full indictment read aloud in full, but you may waive this right and hear only a summary of the indictment involving the relevant parts of the indictment. Mr. Tabakovic, would you please stand for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Zuhdija Tabakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Your date and place of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 16th of February, 1964, in Visegrad, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. What is your present nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, has your family been informed of your transfer to and detention in the United Nations Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, my wife knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We now turn to the Prosecution's indictment. Would you prefer to hear a summary of the charge against you or would you prefer to hear the entire indictment read aloud?

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may be that I can interject at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: It may be that if the full indictment is put to Mr. Tabakovic in private session, that may be the appropriate way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay, if that is what the Defence wants.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm obliged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tabakovic, would you please stand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Pursuant to Rule 62 (A)(iii) of the Tribunal's Rules of Procedure and Evidence, you as the accused have a right to enter a plea of guilty or not guilty on each count. You may enter your plea on any count today or within ten days from your initial appearance here today. In the event that you choose to not enter a plea, either today or within ten days, the Chamber will enter a plea of not guilty on your behalf. Have you discussed this with your duty counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Are you prepared to enter a plea today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I ask you to confine your answer to say either "guilty" or "not guilty" on all accounts or on certain of them, as you wish.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Can you then say what your plea is: Guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty on all six counts of the indictment and the charges against me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated, Mr. Tabakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I remind the Prosecution of its duty under Rule 66(A)(i) to make unavailable to the Defence in a language the accused understands copies of all supporting material which accompany the indictment, as well as prior statements the Prosecutor has obtained from the accused within ten days of this initial appearance. After the Prosecution has turned over these documents to the accused, the Defence has ten days to file its preliminary motions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: I can inform the Court that I met with counsel yesterday and provided him with two copies of the materials, one copy for him and one for his client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm that is correct. The Prosecution did disclose the Rule 66(A)(i) materials yesterday. However, in relation to the time-limit for any preliminary motions, may I just reiterate the fact to the Court that I am duty counsel and, as yet, permanent counsel has not yet been assigned to Mr. Tabakovic and that the ten days would only start running once that has taken place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: May I also add this, that given the intervening period that we have and some of the difficulties that there may be in terms of seeing Mr. Tabakovic, I have discussed this on a preliminary basis with my learned friend Mr. Kremer, on behalf of the Prosecution. And once the decision is taken and permanent counsel is assigned to Mr. Tabakovic, it may be that at that stage it will be appropriate for an application to be made to extend any period for the filing of preliminary motions. It's perhaps premature to make the application now, because we don't know what stage we will be at that stage. But may I just flag-up, as it were, that that may be an application that we will -- or that may be necessary to be made. And my learned friend Mr. Kremer has indicated that, provided it's not an excessive application, that the Prosecution may be sympathetic to such an application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That's on the record now.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: I'm grateful. And may I also add this in relation to the taking of the pleas today. Of course the entering of the pleas could have been adjourned for ten days; but given that it's the Christmas period intervening, there would have been some difficulties having a proper and full consultation of some quite voluminous material with Mr. Tabakovic during that period. And as a consequence, we may well have found ourselves in the same position then as we are today. And it's for that reason that a plea has been entered on that basis today. And I think all parties understand the basis upon which the pleas have been entered today, in order to keep this process moving and complete this phase of the proceedings, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that, Mr. Powles.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tabakovic, would you like to make a statement on any concerns you may have regarding your health or the condition of your detention?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. The Trial Chamber seized of the matter will organise the next appearance and you will be informed of its date in due course. Are there any other matters the parties wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Sorry to take the floor once again, Your Honour, but it's just to put the Court on notice - and again, I've already discussed this with my learned friend Mr. Kremer. There is a hope to put an application in for provisional release sooner rather than later in this case. In order to do that, contact will need to be made with the relevant authorities to see what conditions can be offered to the Court and the Prosecution. But may I just keep the Court apprised that efforts are being made to do that as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's on the record as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. POWLES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If that's all, then we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: adjourned at 2.46 p.m.
